source: Chapter 1: The Structure of Japanese Society
q: What provocative question does the narrator open Volume 1 by asking the reader?
a: He asks whether people are equal or not, demanding the reader's honest opinion.

source: Chapter 1: The Structure of Japanese Society
q: What is the narrator's personal answer to the question of human equality?
a: His answer is no - to be human is to be unequal, and equality does not exist.

source: Chapter 1: The Structure of Japanese Society
q: What examples of society striving for equality does the narrator list?
a: He mentions raising the employment rate for women, creating women-only subway cars, and avoiding the term 'disabled people' so as not to discriminate.

source: Chapter 1: The Structure of Japanese Society
q: Which famous work does the narrator cite when discussing the idea that all people are born equal?
a: He cites the incredibly famous work Gakumon no Susume.

source: Chapter 1: The Structure of Japanese Society
q: According to the famous passage the narrator quotes, what ultimately creates the imbalance in people's positions and status?
a: Education and learning create the imbalance, because encouraging learning produces differences between people.

source: Chapter 1: The Structure of Japanese Society
q: How did the narrator view his future when he entered high school?
a: He had not seriously considered the future at all and only felt joy at being nearly free of obligation.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What nickname did Ayanokouji give to his tactic of pretending to sleep when Horikita approached him?
a: He called it the 'Sleeping Strategy,' which he abandoned within moments when she threatened punishment.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does Horikita threaten Ayanokouji when he pretends not to hear her?
a: She says that if he does not awaken within three seconds she will bestow additional punishment upon him, and later lists harassment like thumbtacks on his chair or stabbing him with her mathematical compass.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What evidence does Ayanokouji claim Horikita left from stabbing him before?
a: He rolls up his sleeve and shows marks on his right forearm, though he admits there is no real evidence proving she was the culprit.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: Who is Horikita Suzune?
a: She is Ayanokouji's classmate in Class D of Tokyo Metropolitan Advanced Nurturing High School, a girl with sharp eyes and long black hair known for her cold demeanor.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: During the bus ride to the entrance ceremony, why does the blond boy refuse to give up his priority seat?
a: He argues that a priority seat carries no legal obligation to move, that standing would waste his energy for no reason, and that he cares only for his own satisfaction.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: Who eventually stands up for the elderly woman on the bus?
a: First a girl in Ayanokouji's school uniform appeals to the passengers, and finally a working woman, unable to bear the guilt, offers her own seat.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What reason does the girl sitting next to Ayanokouji give for not giving up her bus seat?
a: She says giving up the seat would have been pointless, and that she acts according to her own beliefs, which she considers different from merely disliking trouble.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What is the full name of Ayanokouji's high school and who created it?
a: It is Tokyo Metropolitan Advanced Nurturing High School, created by the Japanese government for the express purpose of developing future leaders.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: Where was Ayanokouji's assigned seat in his new classroom?
a: His nameplate marked a seat at the back of the room, near the window.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does Ayanokouji's first attempt at befriending a classmate end?
a: While he agonizes over how to start a conversation, the rotund bespectacled boy in front of him starts talking with another classmate first, beating him to the punch.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does Horikita respond when Ayanokouji introduces himself during the entrance period?
a: She asks if she can refuse to introduce herself and initially keeps her name secret, though she eventually relents and tells him she is Horikita Suzune.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What book is Horikita reading that Ayanokouji notices?
a: She is reading Crime and Punishment.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does Kouenji behave when he enters the classroom on the first day?
a: He puts his feet on his desk, takes out a nail file, and hums while treating his fingernails; within ten seconds more than half the class began drawing away from him.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: Who is the Class D homeroom teacher?
a: Chiyabashira Sae, a woman of about thirty who usually teaches Japanese history and wears her long hair in a ponytail.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What major rules restrict students' lives at the Advanced Nurturing High School?
a: All students must live in on-campus dormitories, contacting anyone outside school is forbidden except in special cases, even family contact requires authorization, and leaving school grounds without permission is strictly forbidden.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What facilities make the school campus comparable to a small city?
a: It has its own karaoke spot, theater, cafe, boutique and more, spread over more than 600,000 square meters.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How do student ID cards and points function at the school?
a: The cards work like credit cards, points act as currency where one point equals one yen, and anything on school premises can be purchased with them.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How many points are students given upon admission, and when are new points deposited?
a: Each student receives 100,000 points at admission, with new points automatically deposited into accounts on the first of every month.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What limitations come with the school's point system?
a: Points cannot be exchanged for cash, all points return to the school after graduation, transferring points to others is allowed, but extorting points from peers is prohibited.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does Chiyabashira explain why students receive such a large point allowance?
a: She says the school evaluates students' talents, and that the amount received reflects the evaluation of their worth and potential from passing the entrance examination.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What statistic makes the school especially prestigious?
a: It boasts a near 100 percent placement rate for students advancing into higher education or entering the workforce, and unlike specialized schools, any student can succeed regardless of field.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: Who breaks the ice for class self-introductions, and what does he share?
a: Hirata Yousuke, an honors-student type, volunteers first and shares that people called him Yousuke in junior high, that his hobby is sports, and that he especially likes soccer.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does Ayanokouji help Inogashira recover when she freezes during her self-introduction?
a: He does not directly - he observes that a classmate telling her to take things slowly rather than shouting encouragement allows her to calm down, breathe, and finish introducing herself.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What does Yamauchi Haruki claim in his self-introduction?
a: He claims he competed in table tennis in elementary school, was the number four ace on his junior high baseball team, got hurt during the inter-high championships, and is undergoing rehab.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: Why is Ayanokouji skeptical of Yamauchi's introduction?
a: Because the inter-high championship is a national competition for high school students, meaning junior high kids like Yamauchi claimed to be should have been ineligible.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What goals does Kushida Kikyou announce in her self-introduction?
a: She says none of her junior high friends made it to the school, so she wants to learn everyone's names and faces right away, become friends with everyone, collect contact information, and make lots of memories together.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does the red-haired delinquent react to being asked to introduce himself?
a: He scowls that they are not little kids, refuses to participate, says he did not come to make friends, and leaves the classroom with several other students.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What does Ike Kanji say in his self-introduction?
a: He declares that he loves girls, hates pretty boys, and is currently in the market for a new girlfriend, preferably a cutie or a beauty.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does Kouenji introduce himself to the class?
a: He announces that as the sole male heir to the Kouenji conglomerate group he will soon carry Japan into the future, addresses his greeting solely to the ladies, and warns he will mercilessly punish anyone who makes him uncomfortable.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does Ayanokouji's own self-introduction go?
a: It is a failure - caught daydreaming, he stammers out that he has no special skills and will try to get along with everyone, drawing applause that feels somewhat like pity, although he secretly feels glad.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What does Horikita buy at the convenience store, and how does Ayanokouji react?
a: She picks only the cheapest shampoo and face wash; Ayanokouji is surprised, expecting girls to fuss over brands, but she explains she does not know when she might need money.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What strange discovery do Ayanokouji and Horikita make in the convenience store corner?
a: They find toiletries and food in a clearance bin labeled 'Free' with a limit of three items per month, which Ayanokouji guesses are emergency relief supplies for students who use up their points.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How does Ayanokouji first befriend Sudou?
a: Sudou forgets his student ID card at the register, and Ayanokouji offers to pay for his noodle cups; grateful, Sudou introduces himself and says he owes him.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: Why does Horikita say she is not afraid of delinquent-looking people like Sudou?
a: She says defenseless people stay away from such types, but if he acted violently she could rebuff him, which is why she does not withdraw.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: How do the second-year students react when they learn Sudou is in Class D?
a: They burst out laughing, say it was a dead giveaway, call the first-years defective products, let them off just for today, and add ominously that they will be in hell soon enough anyway.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What does Ayanokouji notice on the wall outside the convenience store after the confrontation?
a: He discovers two surveillance cameras and mutters that the incident might lead to problems later.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What price detail puzzles Ayanokouji about the convenience store?
a: A noodle cup is priced at 156 yen, and even though payment uses points, all prices are listed in yen, leaving him unsure whether it is expensive or cheap.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: What is Ayanokouji's dormitory room like?
a: He receives a keycard for Room 401; the co-ed dormitory room is about eight tatami mats wide, and it is his first time living alone.

source: Chapter 2: Welcome to the School Life of Your Dreams
q: Why did Ayanokouji really choose this particular high school?
a: Because people cannot contact students without permission there, not even immediate family - he cherishes that freedom and resolves to enjoy his new life without drawing attention.
